features.description: Every trace request is a msgpack POST/PUT to /vX.Y/traces whose single X-Datadog-Trace-Count matches its chunks.
Every trace request names the library: Datadog-Meta-Lang, -Lang-Interpreter, -Lang-Version, and -Tracer-Version, once each.
Every request and span decodes into the native schema without semantic violations.
Every span of a trace chunk carries the chunk's trace id.
Spans carry a name, service, resource, type, error flag, string meta, and numeric metrics.
Trace, span, and parent ids are lossless unsigned 64-bit integers; trace and span ids are nonzero.
Every span was finished: a nonzero start and a duration.
The capture contains a trace root.
Trace roots carry the high 64 trace-id bits in _dd.p.tid; generated ids start with a timestamp.
Every span names its service.
Spans reported under an integration's service name the configured service in _dd.base_service.
Trace roots carry env, spans of the configured service carry version, each with one value.
Spans reported under another service carry no version.
Trace roots name the process: language, runtime-id, and process_id, the same on every span.
Trace roots carry a sampling priority; chunks agree on it; sampling rates appear only on roots.
Traces the tracer starts record the decision maker _dd.p.dm, only on roots or chunk heads.
The configured sampling rule keeps every trace the tracer starts (priority 2, decision maker -3).
A W3C traceparent continues the caller's 128-bit trace under the caller's span.
Datadog headers continue the caller's 128-bit trace under the caller's span.
A trace continued from a sampled traceparent keeps priority 1 and adds no rule decision.
A trace continued from x-datadog-sampling-priority keeps that priority and adds no rule decision.
Server spans carry a valid method and status; only 5xx responses mark them as errors.
Server spans carry span.kind server, component, method, status, route, URL, and user agent.
Server spans record http.url as a full URL with scheme and host.
http.route is the template the request path matched.
Database spans descend from the request's server span.
Database spans are span.kind client.
Database spans name the database in db.system.
A recorded exception is complete: error flag, type, message, and stack.
Every error span is a 5xx server span or records its exception.
Every native field is classified as exact, normalized, or runtime-validated.
